extraction.name: Natural Questions
extraction.description: The Natural Questions corpus is a question answering data set consisting of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine. Annotators are presented with a question along with a Wikipedia page from the top 5 search results, and annotate a long answer and a short answer if present.
extraction.creator: Tom Kwiatkowski, Jennimaria Palomaki, Olivia Redfield, Michael Collins, Ankur Parikh, Chris Alberti, Danielle Epstein, Illia Polosukhin, Jacob Devlin, Kenton Lee, Kristina Toutanova, Llion Jones, Matthew Kelcey, Ming-Wei Chang, Andrew M. Dai, Jakob Uszkoreit, Quoc Le, Slav Petrov
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions are sampled from queries of 8 words or more that were issued to the Google search engine by multiple users.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Long and short answers are set to NULL if no viable candidates exist on the Wikipedia page.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Google search engine queries of 8 words or more and Wikipedia pages.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotation was conducted by a pool of approximately 50 annotators using guidelines and tooling that divide the annotation task, taking an average of 80 seconds per annotation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotation quality was evaluated using post hoc evaluation of correctness for non-null answers by four experts, and k-way annotations (k=25) on a subset of the data to measure precision and recall.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 25 annotations per item on a subset of the data.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors acknowledge potential biases introduced by exclusively using Wikipedia as the source document for answers.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to longer queries (8 words or more) and explicitly excludes "how to" questions and non-Wikipedia domains.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed as a benchmark for open-domain question answering research and natural language understanding, providing specific splits for training, development, and testing.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The data was preprocessed by filtering the query stream using specific heuristics. Only queries of 8 words or more that matched certain syntactic patterns (e.g., starting with specific question words or containing multiple entities) and had a Wikipedia page in the top 5 Google search results were retained.

name.evidence: This paper introduces Natural Questions2(NQ), a new data set for QA research

description.evidence: We present the Natural Questions corpus, a question answering data set. Questions consist of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine. An annotator is presented with a question along with a Wikipedia page from the top 5 search results,and annotates a long answer (typically a paragraph) and a short answer (one or more entities) if present on the page

rai:dataBiases.evidence: We focus on Wikipedia as it is a very important source of factual information, and we believe that stylistically it is similar to other sources of factual information on the Web; however, like any data set there may be biases in this choice.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: The goal of these heuristics is to discard a large proportion of queries that are non-questions, while retaining the majority of queries of 8 words or more in length that are questions. A manual inspection showed that the majority of questions in the data, with the exclusion of question beginning with ‘‘how to’’, are accepted by the filters... Future data collection efforts may introduce shorter queries, ‘‘how to’’ questions, or domains other than Wikipedia.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The public release consists of 307,373 training examples with single annotations; 7,830 examples with 5-way annotations for development data; and a further 7,842 examples with 5-way annotated sequestered as test data... We propose NQ as a new benchmark for research in QA.
